top_news.title: Lebanese military delegation to attend Tampa talks on October 20, seek end of Israeli escalation
top_news.summary: Lebanese President Joseph Aoun announced on Saturday that a Lebanese military delegation will participate in key security talks in Tampa, Florida, on October 20 to present Beirut's demands for an immediate end to Israeli military escalation. The announcement came during high-level discussions between President Aoun and a visiting French delegation led by Minister for Europe and Foreign Affairs Jean-Nol Barrot. During the meeting, the Lebanese leader outlined critical national priorities regarding border stability, international peacekeeping mandates, internal security enforcement, and structural economic reforms. President Aoun strongly condemned ongoing Israeli actions along the southern border, warning that continued hostilities violate prior agreements and obstruct state force deployment. "Israel continues its attacks on southern villages and towns, bulldozing operations, destruction of homes, and preventing farmers from accessing their lands, and has not adhered to the provisions of the framework agreement reached under American sponsorship," the Lebanese Presidency wrote in a post on X. He added that "the continuation of the occupation and tension in the south prevents the Lebanese Army from deploying to the international southern border, in implementation of Resolution 1701." Addressing the future of international peacekeeping forces ahead of their planned 2027 drawdown, President Aoun urged international partners to prevent a security vacuum. "Lebanon wishes to extend the mandate of the international forces or their continuation in their security tasks during the year 2027, designated for their withdrawal, and welcomes, if that proves difficult, any formula that ensures an international presence in the south, prevents a vacuum, and places the Lebanese Army in direct contact with the Israeli Army in the occupied areas," the post read. He emphasised that Beirut "welcomes any French effort within the United Nations and the Security Council to reach a formula consistent with Lebanon's desire to prevent any vacuum." Turning to domestic law enforcement, President Aoun reiterated the government's commitment to disarming unauthorised groups and enforcing the rule of law across the country. "The army and other security forces implement government decisions regarding the extension of state authority, preventing armed manifestations, confiscating weapons and ammunition, and violators are referred to the judiciary, which performs its duty in applying the laws and decisions of the political authority," he wrote. To sustain these internal operations, Aoun called for urgent international backing to properly equip state forces. He stated, "Strengthening the army and equipping it with the necessary gear is essential to enable it and the other security forces to carry out the tasks entrusted to them, and we hope for the convening soon of the international conference to support the army and internal security forces, especially following the positive atmosphere of the preparatory conference in Paris last month." Expressing gratitude to French President Emmanuel Macron for backing key infrastructure and security initiatives, Aoun highlighted the deep historical relationship between the two nations. "President Aoun thanked French President Emmanuel Macron for his decision to resume French commercial flights to Beirut, and for his support of the inclusion of the ports of Beirut and Tripoli in the 'IMEC Economic Corridor Ports Club,' as well as his role in establishing a European mission to provide advisory and support services to the Lebanese Army and Internal Security Forces for a period of three years," the Lebanese presidency wrote. "France's positions express the depth of the deeply rooted historical relations between Lebanon and France, and we hope for the continuation of the French presence in the interest of the two friendly countries," it added. Reaffirming Lebanon's commitment to financial stability and regional alignment, he noted,"We are continuing work to accomplish the economic and financial reforms approved by the government and referred to the Chamber of Deputies.Lebanon is a natural strategic partner for European countries, because its security and stability are part of the security and stability of these countries."French Foreign Minister Jean-Nol Barrot delivered assurances from Paris, reiterating France's steadfast support for Lebanon's territorial integrity and ceasefire agreements. "Conveying the greetings of President Emmanuel Macron and his confirmation of France's standing by Lebanon's side and its continuation in providing support to it in all areas, in cooperation with European partners," the post read. "France's support for Lebanon's sovereignty, stability, and security is steadfast, and it is committed to working for the full implementation of the cessation of hostilities agreement signed on June 26, 2026, and Security Council Resolution 1701," it added. Underlining the necessity of establishing a durable security architecture to avoid volatility in the south, Barrot added, "The necessity of establishing a new international structure to support Lebanon's sovereignty and assist in the redeployment of the Lebanese Armed Forces, and to avoid the emergence of a security vacuum that could have serious consequences, with France prepared to fully assume its role in this framework." He concluded by stressing "the importance of moving forward with the implementation of the essential reforms necessary for the country's recovery, and France's readiness to mobilise its capabilities and respond to urgent humanitarian needs in Lebanon." (ANI)

top_news.title: Trump
top_news.summary: The attack by alleged Israeli settlers on Washington Post Photojournalist Heidi Levine in the West Bank has drawn widespread condemnation. US Secretary of State Marco Rubio said that US President Trump was disturbed by the images of the attack. "We're very disturbed by those images and what we're seeing....the President has been very clear, he's said this repeatedly, he does not want to see friction or crisis going on in the West Bank," he told reporters at Joint Base Andrews. US Ambassador to Israel Mike Huckabee demanded action against the attackers and said the US had called for a full investigation of the incident."Heidi Levine, photojournalist for Washington Post suffered serious injuries from vicious & cowardly attack. Heidi is US Citizen, clear ID as journalist. Details of who under investigation, but those who attacked unarmed reporter should spend YRS in prison. We have called for a full investigation, arrest, and prosecution to the fullest extent of the law to whoever participated in this. Attacking a female photographer is despicable act of terror carried out by masked cowards. Dishonourable act of senseless violence," he said. Israeli President Isaac Herzog condemned the violence and said the despicable behaviour does not represent the values of his country."I just called Washington Post photographer Heidi Levine, who was brutally attacked by violent rioters on Friday. As President of the State of Israel, I strongly condemn this outrageous and shocking violence, both the terrible attack on Heidi and other grave incidents of violence, such as what took place today in Taybeh. I expressed my deepest sorrow to Heidi and apologized for what she went through. The despicable behaviour of the perpetrators of this attack does not represent the citizens or the values of the State of Israel. Israel is a democratic state governed by the rule of law, and it must act with full force against every form of violence. Each incident is being thoroughly investigated, and we await the findings. All government, security, and law enforcement authorities must use every means at their disposal to investigate thoroughly, apprehend these lawbreakers, and bring them to justice with the fullest extent of the law. On behalf of the entire nation, I wish Heidi good health and a speedy recovery," Herzog said. Meanwhile, Heidi Levine underwent surgery at Beilinson Hospital on Saturday after being attacked by Jewish rioters during an olive harvest in the Binyamin region of the West Bank on Friday. Jerusalem Post reported that Levine's condition was described as moderate and that she had sustained injuries to her limbs Speaking to the Committee for Protection of Journalists (CPJ) from her hospital bed, Levine, said that she was "attacked by a gang of masked settlers". "They pushed me to the ground and they were kicking me for, I think at least 10 minutes," she said, confirming that she had identified herself to them as an American journalist. "Hopefully nothing is broken, but I will need stitches in my hand, stitches on my back," she added. Levine said she did not personally see the Israeli military at the scene, but saw tear gas and stunt grenades fired, insinuating that Israeli soldiers must have been there. She also said her bag, camera, and phone were stolen during the attack. "The brutal beating of Heidi Levine is neither isolated nor the first on a journalist covering the olive harvest in the West Bank. It's part of a disturbing pattern of violence and harassment against journalists regardless of their nationalities," said Sara Qudah, CPJ regional director. In September this year, CPJ documented an increase in intensity of settler attacks against journalists in the West Bank. In 2026 alone, CPJ has reviewed at least 16 incidents involving at least 35 local and international journalists that involved physical attacks, harassment, obstruction and intimidation of members of the press. (ANI)

articles.title: Lebanese military delegation to attend Tampa talks on October 20, seek end of Israeli escalation
articles.summary: Lebanese President Joseph Aoun announced on Saturday that a Lebanese military delegation will participate in key security talks in Tampa, Florida, on October 20 to present Beirut's demands for an immediate end to Israeli military escalation. The announcement came during high-level discussions between President Aoun and a visiting French delegation led by Minister for Europe and Foreign Affairs Jean-Nol Barrot. During the meeting, the Lebanese leader outlined critical national priorities regarding border stability, international peacekeeping mandates, internal security enforcement, and structural economic reforms. President Aoun strongly condemned ongoing Israeli actions along the southern border, warning that continued hostilities violate prior agreements and obstruct state force deployment. "Israel continues its attacks on southern villages and towns, bulldozing operations, destruction of homes, and preventing farmers from accessing their lands, and has not adhered to the provisions of the framework agreement reached under American sponsorship," the Lebanese Presidency wrote in a post on X. He added that "the continuation of the occupation and tension in the south prevents the Lebanese Army from deploying to the international southern border, in implementation of Resolution 1701." Addressing the future of international peacekeeping forces ahead of their planned 2027 drawdown, President Aoun urged international partners to prevent a security vacuum. "Lebanon wishes to extend the mandate of the international forces or their continuation in their security tasks during the year 2027, designated for their withdrawal, and welcomes, if that proves difficult, any formula that ensures an international presence in the south, prevents a vacuum, and places the Lebanese Army in direct contact with the Israeli Army in the occupied areas," the post read. He emphasised that Beirut "welcomes any French effort within the United Nations and the Security Council to reach a formula consistent with Lebanon's desire to prevent any vacuum." Turning to domestic law enforcement, President Aoun reiterated the government's commitment to disarming unauthorised groups and enforcing the rule of law across the country. "The army and other security forces implement government decisions regarding the extension of state authority, preventing armed manifestations, confiscating weapons and ammunition, and violators are referred to the judiciary, which performs its duty in applying the laws and decisions of the political authority," he wrote. To sustain these internal operations, Aoun called for urgent international backing to properly equip state forces. He stated, "Strengthening the army and equipping it with the necessary gear is essential to enable it and the other security forces to carry out the tasks entrusted to them, and we hope for the convening soon of the international conference to support the army and internal security forces, especially following the positive atmosphere of the preparatory conference in Paris last month." Expressing gratitude to French President Emmanuel Macron for backing key infrastructure and security initiatives, Aoun highlighted the deep historical relationship between the two nations. "President Aoun thanked French President Emmanuel Macron for his decision to resume French commercial flights to Beirut, and for his support of the inclusion of the ports of Beirut and Tripoli in the 'IMEC Economic Corridor Ports Club,' as well as his role in establishing a European mission to provide advisory and support services to the Lebanese Army and Internal Security Forces for a period of three years," the Lebanese presidency wrote. "France's positions express the depth of the deeply rooted historical relations between Lebanon and France, and we hope for the continuation of the French presence in the interest of the two friendly countries," it added. Reaffirming Lebanon's commitment to financial stability and regional alignment, he noted,"We are continuing work to accomplish the economic and financial reforms approved by the government and referred to the Chamber of Deputies.Lebanon is a natural strategic partner for European countries, because its security and stability are part of the security and stability of these countries."French Foreign Minister Jean-Nol Barrot delivered assurances from Paris, reiterating France's steadfast support for Lebanon's territorial integrity and ceasefire agreements. "Conveying the greetings of President Emmanuel Macron and his confirmation of France's standing by Lebanon's side and its continuation in providing support to it in all areas, in cooperation with European partners," the post read. "France's support for Lebanon's sovereignty, stability, and security is steadfast, and it is committed to working for the full implementation of the cessation of hostilities agreement signed on June 26, 2026, and Security Council Resolution 1701," it added. Underlining the necessity of establishing a durable security architecture to avoid volatility in the south, Barrot added, "The necessity of establishing a new international structure to support Lebanon's sovereignty and assist in the redeployment of the Lebanese Armed Forces, and to avoid the emergence of a security vacuum that could have serious consequences, with France prepared to fully assume its role in this framework." He concluded by stressing "the importance of moving forward with the implementation of the essential reforms necessary for the country's recovery, and France's readiness to mobilise its capabilities and respond to urgent humanitarian needs in Lebanon." articles.title: Trump
articles.summary: The attack by alleged Israeli settlers on Washington Post Photojournalist Heidi Levine in the West Bank has drawn widespread condemnation. US Secretary of State Marco Rubio said that US President Trump was disturbed by the images of the attack. "We're very disturbed by those images and what we're seeing....the President has been very clear, he's said this repeatedly, he does not want to see friction or crisis going on in the West Bank," he told reporters at Joint Base Andrews. US Ambassador to Israel Mike Huckabee demanded action against the attackers and said the US had called for a full investigation of the incident."Heidi Levine, photojournalist for Washington Post suffered serious injuries from vicious & cowardly attack. Heidi is US Citizen, clear ID as journalist. Details of who under investigation, but those who attacked unarmed reporter should spend YRS in prison. We have called for a full investigation, arrest, and prosecution to the fullest extent of the law to whoever participated in this. Attacking a female photographer is despicable act of terror carried out by masked cowards. Dishonourable act of senseless violence," he said. Israeli President Isaac Herzog condemned the violence and said the despicable behaviour does not represent the values of his country."I just called Washington Post photographer Heidi Levine, who was brutally attacked by violent rioters on Friday. As President of the State of Israel, I strongly condemn this outrageous and shocking violence, both the terrible attack on Heidi and other grave incidents of violence, such as what took place today in Taybeh. I expressed my deepest sorrow to Heidi and apologized for what she went through. The despicable behaviour of the perpetrators of this attack does not represent the citizens or the values of the State of Israel. Israel is a democratic state governed by the rule of law, and it must act with full force against every form of violence. Each incident is being thoroughly investigated, and we await the findings. All government, security, and law enforcement authorities must use every means at their disposal to investigate thoroughly, apprehend these lawbreakers, and bring them to justice with the fullest extent of the law. On behalf of the entire nation, I wish Heidi good health and a speedy recovery," Herzog said. Meanwhile, Heidi Levine underwent surgery at Beilinson Hospital on Saturday after being attacked by Jewish rioters during an olive harvest in the Binyamin region of the West Bank on Friday. Jerusalem Post reported that Levine's condition was described as moderate and that she had sustained injuries to her limbs Speaking to the Committee for Protection of Journalists (CPJ) from her hospital bed, Levine, said that she was "attacked by a gang of masked settlers". "They pushed me to the ground and they were kicking me for, I think at least 10 minutes," she said, confirming that she had identified herself to them as an American journalist. "Hopefully nothing is broken, but I will need stitches in my hand, stitches on my back," she added. Levine said she did not personally see the Israeli military at the scene, but saw tear gas and stunt grenades fired, insinuating that Israeli soldiers must have been there. She also said her bag, camera, and phone were stolen during the attack. "The brutal beating of Heidi Levine is neither isolated nor the first on a journalist covering the olive harvest in the West Bank. It's part of a disturbing pattern of violence and harassment against journalists regardless of their nationalities," said Sara Qudah, CPJ regional director. In September this year, CPJ documented an increase in intensity of settler attacks against journalists in the West Bank. In 2026 alone, CPJ has reviewed at least 16 incidents involving at least 35 local and international journalists that involved physical attacks, harassment, obstruction and intimidation of members of the press. (ANI)
